IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON POWER SYSTEMS, VOL. 40, NO. 5, SEPTEMBER 2025 4019
A Static V oltage Stability Enhancement Method for
Power Systems With a High Proportion of V oltage
Source Converters
Y unxin Liu , Liangzhong Y ao , Fellow, IEEE, Siyang Liao , Member , IEEE,J i a nX u , Senior Member , IEEE,
and Fan Cheng , Member , IEEE
Abstract—One of the main characteristics of power systems with
a high proportion of renewable energy is that the power system is
becoming a power system with a high proportion of voltage source
converters (VSCs). Owing to the current limitation of VSCs, the
reactive power regulation range is limited, thus greatly weaken-
ing the effective reactive power reserve and reducing the static
voltage stability. In this paper, the PQ regulation characteristics
of the VSC are ﬁrst analyzed considering the current limitation.
By establishing the PQ characteristic analytical model of a single
grid-connected VSC system, the changes in the system reactive
power reserve and system static voltage stability evolution law
under different penetration ratios of VSCs are analyzed. On this
basis, according to the proposed reactive power support sensitivity
of each source bus, it is proposed to optimally determine the voltage
and effective reactive power reserve of each source bus to realize
effective enhancement of the static voltage stability margin of the
power system with a high proportion of VSCs. Simulation analyses
are carried out in a system with multiple grid-connected VSCs and
an extended IEEE-39 bus system, which validate the effectiveness
and accuracy of the proposed method.
Index Terms —Current limitation, effective reactive power
reserve, high proportion of voltage source converters, reactive
power support sensitivity, static voltage stability.
I. I NTRODUCTION
T
HE deployment of renewable energy such as wind power
and photovoltaics, which are connected to the grid via in-
verters, is increasing worldwide to meet decarbonization targets.
Renewable energy is the backbone of the shift from fossil fuels
to clean and net zero emission systems [1], [2]. In this context,

many synchronous generators are replaced by renewable energy,
and direct-driven wind and photovoltaic power sources with
voltage source converters (VSCs) as grid-connected interfaces
become the main power sources. However, the current limitation
of VSCs results in a smaller reactive power regulation range than
that of a synchronous generator of the same capacity. This will
cause many new problems in the safe and stable operation of
the system, one of which is system static voltage stability [3],
[4], [5].
The connection of VSCs can signiﬁcantly impact the voltage
conditions of consumers and utility equipment, especially under
high penetration levels. These impacts can be positive or negative
depending on the system operating characteristics and the VSC
itself [6], [7]. The impact of VSCs on the voltage stability
phenomenon is an important issue that needs investigation.
V oltage instability is characterized by a progressive de-crease
in voltage magnitude and occurs essentially because of the
system inability to meet a growing demand for reactive power
at certain buses in stressed situations [8]. V oltage instability is
usually of slow nature (minutes or hours), and is driven by the
action of discrete type devices and load variations [9]. The static
voltage instability phenomenon is not new.
However, most studies address the impact of VSCs on short-
term voltage stability and fault-ride-through requirements [10],
[11], [12].I n [13], their study focused on current limitation for
voltage-controlled inverters during overloads caused by poor
transient load sharing between inverters and synchronous gen-
erators in islanded microgrids. In[14], a two-stage simultaneous
control scheme was proposed for improving the transient stabil-
ity of a VSC while considering the current limitation during
the fault state and voltage support after fault clearance. To the
best of the authors’ knowledge, the current literature still lacks
a wider and detailed analysis considering the current limitation
impacts of VSC on static voltage stability with a detailed rep-
resentation of system dynamic. Furthermore, this paper focuses
only on static voltage stability because of the high proportion
of VSCs, and transient voltage problems during fault conditions
are beyond the scope of the proposed model.
Many studies have been carried out on the problem of static
voltage stability with a high proportion of VSCs [15], [16], [17].
However, most studies have focused on constructing stability
indicators and analyzing the change in static voltage stability
with increasing penetration ratio. In [18], on the basis of Norton

current distribution characteristics, a node static voltage sta-
bility index named the H index was constructed, which was
adapted for wind farms. In [19], the load conductivity of the
distribution network was constructed to study the static voltage
stability change under different penetration ratios of distributed
photovoltaics. For the impact of different PCCs of VSCs on
static voltage stability, in[20], the inﬂuence of the penetration of
wind power, different points of common coupling of wind farms,
load growth patterns and other factors on static voltage stability
was analyzed. Overall, these results are based on the current
operating status. However, the impact of the current limitation
on the static voltage stability problem has received less attention.
When the voltage of the points of common coupling of the
VSC is continuously low, the current dispatched by the VSC will
reach the limit value. Moreover, the reactive power dispatched by
the VSC decreases with decreasing reduction. When the system
approaches the point of the voltage collapse, the limitation
characteristic of the VSC will form a positive feedback loop
of the voltage drop-reactive power drop, further deteriorating
the system static voltage stability. The P-V curve reﬂecting the
impacts of the current limitation is shown in the Fig. 1.
Because of the current limitation, the point of voltage collapse
changes from point D to point C, and the distance from the initial
power ﬂow to the point of voltage collapse is shortened from l1
to l2. However, this impact has not yet been quantiﬁed.
It is well known that effective reactive power reserve op-
timization can improve system stability without adding any
other reactive power resources, since reactive power support
is strongly related to voltage instability problems. In terms of
reactive power limit of VSC, in [21], [22], current limits are
used to deﬁne the active and reactive power limits of VSC.
However, no basis is given for the setting of active and reactive
current limits. Recently, the interconnection and interoperability
of VSC standards such as IEEE Std 1547-2018 [23], IEEE Std
2800-2022 [24], GB/T 19964-2024 (China) [25], and GB/T
36547-2024 (China) [26] have been drafted, in [23], [24], [25],
[26], the minimum range for the reactive power capability of
inverter-based resources is required. Based on the standards, we
can get the reactive power capability shall be met for all active
power output levels (including at zero) of the VSC.
The method keeps more reactive power reserves [27], [28],
[29] of the generator, the reactive power weight of which is
larger. One previous study[30] relied on the concept of effective
reactive power reserves and evaluates the impact of generators
on the maximum permissible loading power. Another study[31]
explored the underaddressed topic of reactive power reserve
during the energy transition. In [32], [33], the sensitivity of the
reactive power dispatched by the synchronous generator bus to
the reactive power growth of the load bus was measured.
The above study investigated the value of the reactive power
reserve for a synchronous generator in detail. However, owing
to the current limitation of VSCs, the traditional reactive power
weight is not suitable for systems with a high proportion of
voltage source converters. The inﬂuence on the system reactive
power reserve of grid-connected VSCs will need to consider the
bus voltage immunity.
The contributions of this paper are summarized as follows:
1) To the best of the authors’ knowledge, the impact of
VSC current limitation on static voltage stability has not
been well studied. Many of the new components based on
power electronics will require a dynamic representation to
accurately represent limits. However, proper modeling of
traditional steady-state conditions is also important. The
derivations of the VSC limitations are therefore useful.
Accordingly, the authors attempt to analyze the effect of
VSC current limitation on the static voltage stability.
2) In this paper, a PQ characteristic analytical model of a
single grid-connected VSC system considering the current
limitation is ﬁrst established, and the inﬂuencing mecha-
nism of the current limitation on the static voltage stability
domain of the system is analyzed.
3) By analyzing the PQ regulation characteristics of the VSC
and considering the ability to maintain the static voltage
stability and voltage immunity of generator bus, the reac-
tive power support sensitivity is proposed.
4) It is proposed to optimally determine the voltage and
reactive power of generator bus in base case. The generator
bus with a large reactive power support sensitivity will
retain a more effective reactive power reserve. So, the
static voltage stability margin of the system with a high
proportion of VSCs can be improved more effectively.
The remainder of the paper is organized as follows. Section II
introduces the reactive power regulation range and current lim-
itation of VSCs. Section III presents the static voltage stability
analysis of a single grid-connected VSC system. Section IV
introduces the static voltage stability enhancement method for a
power system with a high proportion of VSCs. Simulations are
provided in Sections V, and VI concludes the paper.
II. A NAL YSIS OF THE PQ CHARACTERISTICS OF VSCS
A. Model of the PQ Characteristics of the VSC

per restricts the discussion only to full-scale converters. If the
current is too high, damage may occur to the semiconductors
in converts. Any control designed to operate under abnormal
grid conditions must adhere to the physical current limitation of
the semiconductors, and a limit is set for the converter current.
Therefore, a VSC is usually connected to a grid via the control
strategy shown in Fig. 2 [34].

Adaptation to Power Systems With a High Proportion of
V oltage Source Converters
The continuation power ﬂow (CPF) [46] is used to calculate
the maximum load active power that the system can carry under
different penetration ratios. During the continuation power ﬂow,
the reformulated set of equations remains well conditioned so
that divergence and error due to a singular Jacobian are not
encountered. As a result, single-precision computations can be
used to obtain power ﬂow solutions at and near the critical point.

represents the load parameter. CPF is easy to implement, and
has a high computational accuracy. So that CPF is a wider
application and more recognized method to calculate voltage
stability boundary [47], [48]. Moreover, CPF is often used as an
exact solution to calibrate the accuracy of the proposed available
methods in [49], [50]. Therefore, the CPF is selected to calculate
the maximum load active power in this paper.
However, in traditional CPF, when a synchronous generator
reactive power reaches the maximum value, the synchronous
generator node is usually transformed from a PV bus to a PQ
bus. It is therefore necessary to improve the CPF to make it
more applicable to the power systems with a high proportion
of VSC. Synchronous generator excitation current limitation
and VSC current limitation are dynamic processes. Considering
their inﬂuence in CPF, it is necessary to combine the reactive
power characteristics of synchronous generator excitation cur-
rent limitation and VSC current limitation with the CPF from
the steady-state condition. This paper proposes an improved
CPF that considers synchronous generator excitation current
limitation and VSC current limitation. The ﬂow is shown in
Fig. 10.
The speciﬁc steps are as follows:
1) Before CPF calculation, calculate the maximum internal
potential Eqmax corresponding to the maximum long-term
maintained excitation current of each synchronous gen-

imum reactive current Iqmax of each VSC. If the reac-
tive power output QGi of the ith synchronous generator

D. Solving Algorithms
The proposed problem is modeled as a nonlinear optimal
reactive power dispatch problem that contains only continuation
variables. The dimensionality of the optimization problem de-
pends on the number of reactive power resources. The interior
point method always searches for the optimal solution inside
the feasible region of the solution, so it can effectively avoid the
situation in which the optimal solution falls on the “spur point”
of the boundary surface and the algorithm fails to converge.
The ﬂow of the reactive power reserve optimization algorithm
based on the interior point method is shown in Fig. 11. When
the reactive power reserve optimization model constructed via
the traditional method and the method proposed in this paper
are solved, both methods adopt the interior point method as the
solution algorithm. The improvement effect is evaluated by the
same evaluation index, which is Pmax. The only difference is
the objective function. The principles of the control variable
approach ensure that the results of the comparative test are
sufﬁciently fair.

V. C ONCLUSION
In this paper, the static voltage stability enhancement method
for a power system with a high proportion of VSCs is studied.
In a single grid-connected VSC system, this paper ﬁrst analyzes
the PQ regulation characteristics of the VSC and synchronous
generator and establishes an analytical model of static voltage
stability by considering the current limitation. The analytical
results show that when the penetration ratio of the VSC reached
40%, the system static voltage stability domain would be re-
duced by 3.76% on average.
By determining the current voltage and effective reactive
power reserve of each source bus according to the reactive power
support sensitivity, the proposed method can effectively improve
the static voltage stability. Two simulation cases have shown that
at medium and high VSC penetration ratios (≥40%), compared
with the traditional method, the static voltage stability enhance-
ment method proposed in this paper is able to better improve
the static voltage stability of a system with a high proportion
of VSCs. In the test system, at penetration ratio of 40%, the
proposed methodology has 2.71% and 2.85% more lift than the
conventional method, respectively. In the extended IEEE-39 bus
system, at high penetration ratio, the proposed methodology has
2.84% and 2.69% more lift than the conventional method does.
However, this paper has not yet considered the intermittence
and variability of VSC resource power output. Non-continuous
variable reactive power compensation devices such as casting
capacitors are not considered. In future work, the model will
be transformed into a mixed-integer linear programming model.
And an intraday reactive power reserve optimization method can
be explored for adoption in hard real-time systems.
